properties.Lithology, structures, paleowind: Green siltstones intercalated with whitish sandstones and micritic limestones. Pyroclastic and lava flows (Las Conchas Basalt) occur associated with sedimentary deposits.
properties.Fossil occurrences: pipid frogs, plant remains and clupeiform fish

properties.Dating evidence: Calcareous nannofossils (Zones CC25A, CC25B, and CC25C), Foraminifera (Gansserina gansseri Zone)
properties.Lithology, structures, paleowind:
Alternating mudstones/watckestones (light grey tabular beds, massively or intensely bioturbated, presence of molluscs, vegetable remains, sulfide nodules, carbonate concretions, and fractures filled with calcite. Low to very low clay content) and argillaceous mudstones/watckestones (deep grey tabular beds with intense bioturbation, presence of molluscs, pyrite and carbonate nodules. High to very high clay content)

Structures are rhythmic bedding, meteorological tidal channels, bioturbations, fitted fabric, stylolites and karstic features.
properties.Paleoenvironment: Sedimentological analysis suggests a quiet, warm water depositional environment with moderate (below wave-base) depth. Foraminifera assemblages indicate deposition in an outer neritic to upper bathyal setting of a pelagic carbonate ramp system. The low diversity of the ichnofauna and abundance of Thalassinoides suggests oxygen depleted bottom-water conditions, with low do moderate energy.

properties.Geochemistry data:
d18O and d13C: Strong positive correlation with Mg, indicating heavy diagenetic alteration and thus not representative of the original oceanographic signal.

Negative correlation between Ca and SI

High phosphate concentrations (1.5%) in the 24.0?1.0m interval.
properties.Climate assignment leading evidence: Geochemical and sedimentological analysis indicate the presence of a warm and dry environment for the basin at this moment, based on the very low siliciclastic input which led to the development of a pelagic carbonate ramp.
